title: Hammock localization presents universal infinity localization
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category and let $W$ be a wide subcategory, containing every identity. Enlarge universes so that $\mathcal C$ and all the diagram categories below are small. The hammock localization $L^H(\mathcal C,W)$ is a category enriched in simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with the same objects as $\mathcal C$. Its mapping simplicial set from $x$ to $y$ has as $k$-simplices reduced commutative hammocks of width $k$: $k+1$ rows of finite zigzags from $x$ to $y$, all vertical maps pointing down and belonging to $W$, identity vertical maps at the endpoints, all horizontal maps in any column pointing in the same direction, leftward horizontal maps in $W$, adjacent columns pointing in opposite directions, and no column consisting entirely of identities. Faces and degeneracies delete or repeat rows and then reduce by composing adjacent like-directed columns and deleting identity columns. Composition concatenates and reduces hammocks. Choose a fibrant replacement of this enriched category that induces weak homotopy equivalences on mapping simplicial sets, so its mapping objects are Kan complexes. The homotopy coherent nerve of this replacement is an infinity category $\mathcal L$ and the induced $q:N\mathcal C\to\mathcal L$ is a universal infinity localization at $W$: for every infinity category $\mathcal E$, precomposition identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal E)$ with the full infinity subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ on functors sending $W$ to equivalences. Here the ordinary nerve has composable strings as simplices; the homotopy coherent nerve has in degree $n$ enriched functors from the simplicial coherent realization of $\Delta^n$; and an infinity category is a simplicial set filling every inner horn. In particular $L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x,y)$ represents $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(qx,qy)$, its length-one hammocks represent $q$ on actual maps, and these comparisons are natural for functors preserving $W$, respecting composition and its homotopies.
